issues.evidence: F1: CloudCredentials S3 broken. filesystem.py _ALLOWED_SECRET_OPTIONS['S3'] accepts access_key_id/secret_access_key but configure() interpolates them verbatim into CREATE SECRET (TYPE S3, ...); DuckDB 1.5.x expects KEY_ID/SECRET -> BinderException Unknown parameter 'access_key_id'. Fix: map access_key_id->KEY_ID, secret_access_key->SECRET, session_token->SESSION_TOKEN at SQL-build time; keep documented names; keep region/endpoint_url/url_style/use_ssl passthrough. Re-verify option names for S3/AZURE/GCS on DuckDB 1.5.5. Add focused injection tests per AGENTS source-adapter doctrine.
issues.root_cause: DuckDB 1.5.x renamed cloud-secret option names; filesystem.py allowlist still carried the legacy snake_case names (access_key_id etc.) and interpolated them verbatim into CREATE SECRET, so every provider raised BinderException on 1.5.5. AZURE account_key and GCS service_account_json were removed upstream entirely.
issues.resolution: fhir4ds/sources/filesystem.py: replaced _ALLOWED_SECRET_OPTIONS with _SECRET_OPTION_ALIASES (snake_case->native names per provider, probed live on 1.5.5), _REMOVED_SECRET_OPTIONS (AZURE account_key, GCS service_account_json -> typed ValueError with guidance), and _AZURE_SERVICE_PRINCIPAL_KEYS (emits PROVIDER service_principal clause). configure() maps, sorts, and quote_sql_literal's values. Injection tests kept.
issues.verified_in: tests/unit test_filesystem.py 49/49 (sources tree 230/230); live duckdb 1.5.5 probes: S3/GCS-HMAC/AZURE-connstr/AZURE-SP secrets register, removed opts ValueError, injection blocked

issues.spec_citation: CQL 1.5 Appendix B section 19.31 Union (Interval): interval union returns the merged interval when operands overlap or meet, null otherwise; dynamic FHIR Period operands are intervals, not lists.
issues.evidence: E1.period union Interval[...] raised DuckDB BinderException 'Cannot mix values of type VARCHAR[] and VARCHAR in CASE expression'; E1.period union E2.period list_concat'd Period JSON strings instead of merging. Root cause: _translate_union_op ran _is_fhir_interval_expression on POST-promotion operands; _union_operand_as_list's last-resort _promote_fhirpath_text_list rewrote fhirpath_text(res,'period') (interval-recognized) to from_json(fhirpath(...),'["VARCHAR"]') (not recognized), dropping the union into list semantics.
issues.root_cause: _operators.py _translate_union_op interval detection ran after operand list-promotion; the promoted from_json shape is not in _is_fhir_interval_expression's recognizer set.
issues.resolution: Capture pre-promotion operands (_left_pre_promotion/_right_pre_promotion) in _translate_union_op; interval detection ORs the pre-promotion check; intervalUnion receives the interval-shaped operand variant (pre-promotion fhirpath_text Period JSON when the promoted side is not interval-parseable).
issues.verified_in: fhir4ds/cql/duckdb/tests/integration/test_evol_it7_domain3_skeptic.py (4 union tests, dual-value checks); interval parity suites 44 pass.

issues.spec_citation: CQL 1.5 grammar: expand/collapse bare form takes a full expression operand (identifier, interval selector, or property path) followed by optional per-quantity.
issues.evidence: parse_expression('expand E1.period per day') raised ParseError 'trailing tokens: PER'; 'collapse E1.period per day' identical. parse_primary_expression stopped after the primary E1, leaving .period for the outer postfix chain which then dangled at PER.
issues.root_cause: parser.py:2326-2334 bare expand/collapse branch used parse_primary_expression for the operand; property chains after the primary were never consumed inside the branch.
issues.resolution: Bare branch now uses parse_postfix_expression (primary + DOT/invocation/indexer/query postfix loop) which stops cleanly at PER.
issues.verified_in: test_evol_it7_domain3_skeptic.py TestBareExpandCollapsePropertyPathEvolIt7Skeptic (4 tests); CQL unit tree 1656 pass.

issues.spec_citation: CQL 1.5 Appendix B section 10.x stored-list consumer doctrine (CQL-18 HISTORIAN family): defines whose CTE value column holds the whole element list must be marked stores_list_value so Count aggregates elements and First/Last LIST_EXTRACT the list.
issues.evidence: define X: expand Interval[@2024-01-01,@2024-01-05] per day -> Count(X)=1 (row count) instead of 5; First(X)='[' (character-sliced the JSON array text); inline Count(expand ...) BinderException list_aggr(VARCHAR, STRING_LITERAL) via list_count over the expand_points JSON text.
issues.root_cause: _is_list_returning_sql name set and the translator define-meta chain did not recognize expand/expand1/expand_points/expand_points1/collapse_intervals/collapse_intervals_per UDF forms; the CTE physically stores the JSON array string but no marker was set, so consumers treated it as a scalar/rows value.
issues.resolution: (a) translator.py: FunctionRef(expand/collapse) define bodies set _definition_is_navigation_list (stored-list, List<Any>, PATIENT_SCALAR); (b) _utils.py _is_list_returning_sql recognizes the 6 UDF names; (c) _functions.py _translate_aggregate_pre stored-list branch routes Count->json_array_length and others->from_json when the define AST is expand/collapse; (d) _translate_first_last_list_define_pre wraps the reference in from_json; (e) _wrap_list_aggregate JSON-list guard returns json_array_length for COUNT over the 6 UDF names (inline path); (f) _lists.py First/Last JSON wrap extended to the expand family. FOLLOW-UP (same iteration): recognizing the 6 UDF names in _is_list_returning_sql made First/Last sort-by queries over collapse JSON hit list_sort(VARCHAR) (CMS135/144/145/645/646 BinderException, DQM 42/47); fixed by parsing JSON-array-string sources via from_json BEFORE list_sort/list_extract in both _lists.py First/Last branches. Final gate 2832/2832 incl. DQM 47/47.
issues.verified_in: test_evol_it7_domain3_skeptic.py TestExpandCollapseStoredListConsumersEvolIt7Skeptic (5 tests: Count 5, First '2024-01-01', multi-interval Count 5, collapse Count 1, inline Count 5); list parity suites 66 pass.; master gate 2832/2832 (ViewDef 144, FHIRPath 935, CQL 1706, DQM 47) after sort-by follow-up fix.

issues.spec_citation: CQL 1.5 Appendix B Distinct (List<T>): returns the list with duplicates removed; the query-return operand is a per-patient element list, not an aggregate context.
issues.evidence: distinct ([Observation] O return O.status) raised BinderException 'column patient_id must appear in the GROUP BY clause' — the generic Distinct fallback wrapped the rows-shaped subquery in LIST() ('Distinct'(LIST((SELECT ...)))) placing an aggregate next to the outer _pt.patient_id projection. Verified pre-existing on clean HEAD via git-checkout bisect.
issues.root_cause: _translate_distinct_expression generic fallback (_lists.py) had no rows-source coercion; LIST() aggregate in scalar projection context.
issues.resolution: Rows-shaped sources (SQLSelect/SQLSubquery) coerce via _coerce_query_rows_to_list to the per-patient list subquery before the Distinct wrap (single-value-column branch).
issues.verified_in: fhir4ds/cql/duckdb/tests/integration/test_evol_it8_domain3_historian.py (2 tests incl. SQL-shape regression assert); list parity suites 66 pass.

issues.spec_citation: CQL 1.5 §19.27 (Query aggregate clause): folds the source rows into a single value per patient.
issues.evidence: [Observation] O aggregate T starting 0: T + 1 raised BinderException 'Subquery returns 6 columns - expected 1' — list_prepend(0, (SELECT * FROM Observation)) over the multi-column rows CTE. Conditional bodies (T + if O.status=... ) then failed +(JSON/VARCHAR, INTEGER). Verified pre-existing on clean HEAD.
issues.root_cause: (a) The single-source scalar aggregate path fed the raw rows-shaped SELECT * into list_reduce; (b) no patient correlation (rows would leak across patients); (c) element/accumulator physical types did not bind (JSON elements, INTEGER starts); (d) _infer_row_shape had no aggregate branch so the define was classified RESOURCE_ROWS and projected through json_extract.
issues.resolution: _query.py aggregate lowering: rows-shaped sources materialize the patient-correlated per-patient resource element list (list_transform CAST VARCHAR), lambda element param uses the _lt_<alias> prefix convention so Property access routes through fhirpath, numeric literal starting values bind the accumulator alias as TRY_CAST DECIMAL(38,8) and the prepended start casts to VARCHAR; inference.py classifies aggregate queries PATIENT_SCALAR. Helper _patient_correlated_where added.
issues.verified_in: test_evol_it8_domain3_historian.py (5 tests: count fold, conditional fold, literal-list control, cross-patient isolation, shape classification); CQL unit 1656 pass.

issues.spec_citation: CQL 1.5 Appendix B First/Last (List<T> element extraction); expand/collapse UDF output is a JSON array string.
issues.evidence: First(collapse {...} per day) returned '[' and First(expand ...) likewise — the generic _translate_first/_translate_last emitted LIST_EXTRACT(<JSON VARCHAR text>, 1), character-slicing the JSON (it7's from_json wrap existed only in the query-source and stored-list-define paths). start of First(collapse ...) therefore evaluated to None.
issues.root_cause: _functions.py _translate_first/_translate_last lacked the JSON-array-string source handling for direct inline expand/collapse FunctionRef arguments.
issues.resolution: New _json_list_source_for_extract helper wraps the 6 expand/collapse UDF names in from_json(...,'["VARCHAR"]') before LIST_EXTRACT in both First and Last.

issues.spec_citation: CQL 1.5 §19.27 aggregate over a query whose source is an expand (JSON array string element list).
issues.evidence: (expand Interval[...] per day) D aggregate T starting 0: T + 1 raised BinderException list_concat(INTEGER[], VARCHAR) — the aggregate fold received the raw expand_points JSON text with an INTEGER start prepended.
issues.root_cause: _query.py aggregate coercion only handled SQLSelect/SQLSubquery rows sources; expand/collapse SQLFunctionCall JSON sources reached list_prepend unparsed.
issues.resolution: Aggregate lowering parses JSON-array-string sources via from_json before the fold and marks _agg_element_is_json (the _lt_ alias + DECIMAL/VARCHAR start-cast machinery from QA-013 applies).

issues.title: { <query> } braced-query list selector broken in every consumer (eCQM pattern)
issues.root_cause: CQL 1.5 listSelector grammar allows a query element ('{' (query | expression)? '}'). _translate_list_expression wrapped the Query element in SQLArray producing [(SELECT * FROM ...)] — a multi-column rows subquery in scalar array position. exists/Count/First/Last/singleton-from/distinct/flatten/indexer/Sum all raised BinderException (Subquery returns 2 columns) or scalar-subquery-multi-row errors; legally-authored eCQM-style exists ({ [Condition: VS] C where ... }) crashed whole measures.
issues.resolution: Three-part fix: (1) _translate_list_expression (_lists.py): single-Query list selectors whose translation is rows-shaped (SQLSubquery/SQLSelect) coerce via _coerce_query_rows_to_list to a per-patient LIST with patient correlation (_patient_correlated_where, QA-013 convention) and resource-valued star-shape projection (where-only queries project row.resource, matching the unbraced query-define path); list-source contexts (aggregate folds over unnest elements) keep the SQLArray single-element wrap (pre-existing shape; RolledOutIntervals depends on it). (2) _is_list_valued_projection idempotence guard in _coerce_query_rows_to_list (_utils.py): projections already evaluating to list(...) are not re-wrapped (First over the coerced subquery previously double-wrapped list(list(...))). (3) _translate_exists_expression: exists ({ query }) unwraps to the plain query EXISTS form (the LIST coercion shape breaks the correlated-EXISTS rewrite).
issues.verified_in: fhir4ds/cql/duckdb/tests/integration/test_evol_it10_domain4_skeptic.py (13 tests); focused suites 103 passed (list part1/part2, it7, it8, interval part3); CQL unit 1656; master gate 2832/2832 (first gate run caught RolledOutIntervals regression 2831/2832 — fixed by the rows-shaped guard before final gate).

issues.title: Chained with-clauses: later such_that referencing earlier with alias raises BinderException
issues.root_cause: The with-clause loop in _translate_query (_query.py) pushed/popped a scope PER CLAUSE: each with alias registration was popped before later clauses translated, and each clause emitted a FLAT correlated EXISTS ANDed into the outer WHERE. A later such_that referencing an earlier with alias (CMS71-style: with E1 such that ... with V such that V.effective during E1.period) emitted E1 references no FROM could bind (Referenced table E1 not found). 19 real eCQM files in the test corpus use >=2 with-clauses in one query.
issues.resolution: Rewrote the with-clause handling: one shared scope for the whole chain (all with aliases registered and visible to later such_that translations), then clauses compose NESTED — clause i>1 EXISTS lands in clause i-1 EXISTS subquery WHERE with its patient correlation pointing at the PREVIOUS clause alias (transitively linked to the outer patient through clause 1). Single-with queries produce the same flat shape as before (no behavior change; 715-test integration suite + DQM 47/47 green).
issues.verified_in: test_evol_it11_domain4_historian.py (4 tests incl. SQL-shape nested-EXISTS assertion); full CQL integration 715 passed/5 skipped/1 xfailed; master gate 2832/2832.

issues.title: Braced-query list selector as query source ({query}) Alias produced broken derived tables
issues.root_cause: ({ <query> }) Z <clauses> — the iteration-10 coerced LIST subquery fell through the query-source handling to the nested-query-source branch, which rebuilt a derived table with self-referential patient correlation (Referenced table _cql_list_source/_list not found).
issues.resolution: Query-source path in _query.py: a ListExpression AST source (single element) whose SQL is the coerced LIST subquery UNNESTs like the array source, alias binding + projected patient_id. FIRST VERSION lacked the AST guard (any list-valued subquery source hit it) and regressed DQM CMS0334/CMS71/CMS832 to 85-96% — the gate caught it; guard narrowed to isinstance(source_expr_node, ListExpression) restored 100%.
issues.verified_in: test_evol_it12_domain4_explorer.py (2 tests); nullological+list_part2+structural 87 passed; DQM spot CMS0334/CMS71/CMS832 100%; master gate 2832/2832.

issues.title: Audit-mode contains over dynamic multi-valued FHIR properties emits list_contains(VARCHAR) binder errors
issues.root_cause: The audit fast path in _list_contains_call (_operators.py, added to work around a DuckDB struct_pack binder bug with the CQLListContainsEq macros inside audit_leaf/audit_and chains) emitted raw list_contains(list_sql, ...) WITHOUT the CQL-18 fhirpath_text -> from_json(fhirpath(...)) full-list promotion — list_contains received the scalar first-node VARCHAR.
issues.resolution: Promote via _promote_fhirpath_text_list before the raw builtin call in the audit fast path. from_json(fhirpath(...)) is a plain scalar expression (no macro expansion), so the original struct_pack binder workaround still holds. Verified: audit-mode population SQL executes with correct results and causal evidence (findings.target names the winning resources, e.g. Encounter/eB, Condition/cB in the Denominator narrative).
issues.verified_in: test_evol_it25_domain9_skeptic.py (3 tests); audit suite 31/31; master gate 2832/2832.

issues.title: audit_mode=full: Count(<rows-define>) >= N raised multi-row scalar subquery errors
issues.root_cause: Two audit-layer defects: (1) cte_manager evidence-JOIN fan-out was aggregated per-patient ONLY for bare SQLAuditStruct expressions — comparison-wrapped audit expressions (COALESCE((SELECT __pre_X...), audit_leaf(false))) fell through to the raw N-row JOIN form; (2) _synthesize_target_from_resource_select built the audit-target twin as a scalar subquery returning one row per matching resource — N-row sources (Count over rows defines) crashed with More than one row returned by a subquery.
issues.resolution: (1) Aggregate EVERY evidence-JOIN shape (ANY_VALUE + group_by patient_id — the audited value is patient-deterministic); (2) synthesize the target as array_to_string(list_sort(list_distinct(list(resource-id-expr))), ",") — always exactly one row; multi-winner evidence renders comma-joined sorted ids (Encounter/e1,Encounter/e2); single-row sources unchanged.
issues.verified_in: test_evol_it27_domain9_explorer.py (3 tests incl. winner-evidence assertion); audit suite 31/31; adversarial audit-full composition (count-exclusion + numerator-exclusion + stratifier) attribution correct; master gate 2832/2832.
